definition: A woman who either died or nearly died from a pregnancy complication - a maternal death or a maternal near-miss.
A woman who survived a life-threatening complication in pregnancy, childbirth, or the weeks after.
The death of a woman during pregnancy or within 42 days of its end, from a cause related to the pregnancy.
The share of severe-outcome women who died - here, deaths divided by all near-miss-plus-death cases.
Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births in a facility over a set period.
Stillbirths plus deaths in the first week of life.
Bleeding from the birth canal before delivery, in later pregnancy.
High blood pressure in pregnancy, including pre-eclampsia and eclampsia.
Care that follows the agreed emergency treatment steps, delivered by a skilled team.
Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care - the core services for handling birth emergencies.
The number of times a woman has given birth before.
